title: Airline swapped direct Phuket flights for 11-hour layover: pays ₹70,000

slides.head: Airline swapped direct Phuket flights for 11-hour layover: pays ₹70,000
What happened
slides.body: The family paid ₹1,16,477 for four round-trip tickets (June 6–13, 2026); on May 21 the airline cancelled them and rebooked via Bengaluru, with an 11-hour halt on return.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: The airline cited winter schedule changes and operational reasons but did not substantiate why confirmed flights were cancelled, the commission found.

slides.head: Compensation awarded
slides.body: The airline's counsel appeared, but it never filed a written reply within 45 days, so its right to respond was closed.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: The family also paid ₹2,949 extra for baggage, and had non-refundable Phuket hotel bookings.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: Whether the airline appeals the order. Ask: What assistance are airlines required to give during long halts caused by rescheduling?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

Airline swapped direct Phuket flights for 11-hour layover: pays ₹70,000

A Telangana consumer commission held an airline liable for deficiency in service after it cancelled a family's booked non-stop Hyderabad–Phuket flights and moved them to connecting flights.

Why it matters: The airline cited winter schedule changes and operational reasons but did not substantiate why confirmed flights were cancelled, the commission found.

Source: Times of India. Image: Times of India
